question: Can sender and atomic receiver learn to omit a redundant bit, generalize to an unseen exactly-one wiring and retain the fourth bit under independence?
inputs: Nine raw bits to sender; four public groups of signed incidence rows to both; physical bits and eventual question only to receiver.
forbidden_inputs: Query names, true answer tables, omission labels, raw input or selected wire IDs in the receiver, hidden test-time optimization, refits on held wiring.
mapping: Fit two pairs of public sender/decoder policies from terminal answers and length using elementary Boolean program search. Strict and varied training use the same search.
primary_observable: Exhaustive full-answer accuracy and physical packet width versus independent answer-vector count on every held wiring.
comparators_or_controls: Copy-only limit, strict any-only versus varied training, all port permutations, matched sign-count rewiring, fourth source substitution, input parity holdout, three-bit collision for independent answers.
resource_budget: Two exploratory fits, six or 36 training wirings on 256 even tables. Test 168 held wirings on all 512 tables and four ports. CPU shared runner.
first_executable_signal: A correct three-bit packet can service all four original questions if the decoder can compute the omitted answer.
stop_rule: Run both declared checkpoints as frozen, preserve failed or nonminimal outputs and report finite scope.
